fr-inao-a146.atlas_note: Chardonnay grown around the town of Chablis in the Yonne, the northern outpost of Burgundy. The best sites lie on Kimmeridgian marl with fossil oyster shells, which many link to the wine's saline, chalky edge.

fr-inao-a147.atlas_note: One appellation made of seven climats on a single south-west facing slope above the town of Chablis, on the right bank of the Serein: Blanchot, Bougros, Les Clos, Grenouilles, Preuses, Valmur and Vaudésir. Chardonnay on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.

fr-inao-a148.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a148.atlas_note: Grand cru of Gevrey-Chambertin and one of the most powerful, long-lived red Burgundies. Pinot Noir on a gentle mid-slope of limestone and marl, just below the woods. Long associated with Napoleon, who is said to have drunk little else. The mapped area also includes Chambertin-Clos de Bèze, whose wine may be sold as Chambertin.

fr-inao-a149.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a149.atlas_note: Grand cru adjoining Chambertin to the north. The monks of the Abbey of Bèze planted a vineyard here in the 7th century, which makes it one of the oldest named sites in Burgundy. It may legally be sold as Chambertin, but not the other way round.

fr-inao-a150.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a150.atlas_note: Village famed for the most perfumed and silky reds of the Côte de Nuits. Limestone-rich soils with little clay. Les Amoureuses is its most celebrated premier cru.

fr-inao-a151.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a151.atlas_note: Grand cru south of Clos de Bèze, below the road. Shallow soils give a perfumed, more delicate Chambertin style.

fr-inao-a153.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a153.atlas_note: The largest grand cru of Gevrey, below Chambertin across the Route des Grands Crus. Wine from Mazoyères-Chambertin may be sold under this name, which is why Charmes is far more common on labels. The mapped area therefore includes Mazoyères.

fr-inao-a154.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a154.atlas_note: Southern neighbour of Puligny, with a share of Montrachet and Bâtard and all of Criots-Bâtard. Known for whites, it also produces a good share of red.

fr-inao-a155.atlas_note: Jura appellation for vin jaune only: Savagnin aged at least six years under a veil of yeast, without topping up, and sold in the 62 cl clavelin bottle.

fr-inao-a157.atlas_note: Grand cru directly above Montrachet in Puligny. Steeper and stonier, it gives a tighter, more mineral wine.

The château is the seat of the Confrérie des Chevaliers du Tastevin.

fr-inao-a164.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a164.atlas_note: Grand cru that gave its name to the village of Morey-Saint-Denis. Known for finesse and aromatic lift rather than sheer weight.

fr-inao-a165.grapes: Chardonnay B/Pinot Blanc B/Pinot Gris G/Pinot Noir N
fr-inao-a165.atlas_note: The largest grand cru of Burgundy and the only red grand cru of the Côte de Beaune, on the hill of Corton shared by Aloxe-Corton, Ladoix-Serrigny and Pernand-Vergelesses. A climat name can be added, such as Corton Bressandes or Corton Clos du Roi.

fr-inao-a166.atlas_note: White grand cru on the upper slopes of the hill of Corton, planted with Chardonnay. Tradition links it to the emperor Charlemagne, who is said to have owned vines here.
